posts.title: How we do forensics, and where it breaks: the Hawthorne method, open for argument
posts.description: Three AI reviewers together caught 8 of 10 errors planted in one essay, no more than the strongest reviewer alone. Hawthorne reports that all three caught the two missed errors in a follow-up that supplied two relevant records.

posts.title: The Binance heist, Part Two: the route to the signing service, and where the assets went
posts.description: Within nine minutes of the first withdrawal, the first address to receive stolen funds sent 700,000,000 USDT tokens to two other addresses. Binance describes a fake job interview and misuse of an internal AI tool but not how the attacker reached its signing service.

posts.title: The Binance heist, Part One: fifty valid signatures, one that landed, and an authority that stood for 3 hours 49 minutes
posts.description: An attacker moved assets seven times after a signed instruction let a Binance wallet run the attacker’s code. Automated deposits kept refilling the wallet, including a transfer of 200,000,000 USDT that the attacker took 72 seconds after it arrived.
